scenes.title: 큰 프리뷰와 전체 모듈 구성
scenes.feature: The large preview is the starting point; all constituent modules stay visible.
scenes.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one exceptionally clear, visually distinctive yet realistically implementable Windows desktop application reference screen for DEPTH AI. Edge-to-edge software interface, landscape 16:10, high-resolution carefully typeset. No device mockup, no photographed monitor, no people, no Unity, no MR, no floating spatial environment.
This is a coherent desktop program for seeing how a visible interface is built from actual source modules and using Meta AI to explain, split and integrate code. The PRIMARY surface MUST be a LARGE interactive application preview, taking approximately 48% of the usable screen width and 75% height, with readable content, NOT a sidebar thumbnail. Beside it show all modules forming the selected feature together, with a clear pinned source reading surface. User must immediately see "click an element in the preview -> its real modules and source". Do not hide preview behind graph or tiny inspector.
Design language: warm ivory Field Guide editorial surface, refined serif section headings, clean highly legible English sans-serif UI labels, subtle paper folder module bodies and restrained indigo/sage/terracotta role colors. Role silhouettes: folder-like logic modules, state capsules, asset frames, diamond validation gates. Only 1-2 connection ports per body. Same function appears once and shared incoming lines converge on it. Strong graphic modules, never a generic KPI-card dashboard. Front-facing flat readable text, subtle 2px paper depth, generous 24px gutters, no overlapping text/icons/lines, no clipping, no microtext. Sparse orthogonal directed wires behind bodies, selected path indigo, contextual relations pale. Empty crossings are NOT junctions. Dotted lines mean declared bindings/ownership, not calls.
Shared application chrome for this entire series: top left DEPTH AI wordmark, project selector "Checkout", nav "Explore", "Explain", "Split", "Merge", "Assets", "Review". Top right compact "Meta" action and "Light / Dark" switch. Small secondary view tabs "Field Guide", "Route Atlas", "Orbit". Persistent understated footer "DESIGN REFERENCE • Illustrative source data". Main preview white framed "Project preview", button "Expand", helper "Select any text, value or image". No giant promotional heading, no floating statistics, no claims of verified execution.
Sample product preview: title "Your cart", small "CHECKOUT", two consistent product images: cream matte ceramic mug on a warm neutral background; green monstera in a warm ivory cylindrical pot. Product names "Ceramic mug" and "Indoor plant", prices "48.00" and "72.00". Summary "Subtotal 120.00", "Discount -24.00", strongly legible "Total 96.00", small "WELCOME20", indigo "Apply coupon" button. Every text and image visibly looks individually inspectable on hover, but not every item heavily outlined.
Right workspace "Feature composition": single ApplyCoupon coordinator, IsValid validation diamond, CalculateTotal shared pricing folder, SetTotal writer, Read presentation, Subtotal state capsule 120, DiscountPercent state capsule 20, Total state capsule 96, tiny cart/pricing/view reference capsules, two framed assets mug.png and plant.png. All 13 are visible together, not a solitary selected module. Four prominent CALLS go from ApplyCoupon to IsValid, CalculateTotal, SetTotal and Read; CalculateTotal REFERENCES DiscountPercent. No added CalculateTotal->Read CALL. Keep remaining context wires understated and do not pretend this is runtime order. A restrained selected line exposes type and source location in its own clear strip.
Below/right compact but readable source excerpt "CheckoutController.cs" with EXACT line "cart.SetTotal(pricing.CalculateTotal(cart.Subtotal));" and a "Read source" control. Avoid showing entire files at tiny type. User scenario: initial explore view with full live-looking preview and complete composition. Preview must be the first thing the eye sees and visibly as important as the module graph. Produce ONE finished reference image, not a collage or a written explanation.
